Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No documented integration of farmer registries or agricultural input systems with a national data exchange platform. Score 1: not integrated.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) did not match the Comments text, which already concluded a score of 1 (not integrated). Both originally cited sources were fetched and support a picture of fragmented government systems with no agriculture data exchange integration. A December 2025 announcement by the Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries of a planned 'integrated digital ecosystem' (single portal for producer/plot registration, input certification and traceability) postdates the April 2025 Data Governance Diagnostic and shows the sector has moved from 'no plans' to an explicit planning stage. Revised Value Code to 2 (Planned).
revised_comments: Mozambique's Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries announced in December 2025 the development of an integrated digital ecosystem intended to bring together producer and plot registration, input certification, traceability and market-access services onto a single portal. This remains at the planning and design stage: there is no evidence of farmer registries, input voucher systems or land registration data being technically integrated with a national government data exchange platform. The 2025 World Bank/African Development Bank Data Governance Diagnostic likewise found government information systems in Mozambique to be fragmented, relying on ad hoc file-sharing rather than structured interoperability.

Definition: Integration of learner records, academic credentials, enrollment data, and scholarship/bursary systems
Comments: No documented integration of education systems with a national data exchange platform. The NUIC is planned to eventually incorporate all citizen documents including student records. Score 2: planned.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) conflicted with the Comments, which already concluded a score of 2 (planned). This is confirmed: the Ministry of Education's Education Technology Plan (Plano Tecnológico da Educação, 2019 revision, covering 2011-2026) contains an explicit programme (5.2, 'Interoperabilidade com os sistemas do MINEDH') to connect the ministry's information systems with other government institutions, and a DHIS2-based EMIS pilot exists in two provinces, but there is no evidence of an operational link between learner records and a national government data exchange. Revised Value Code to 2 (Planned).
revised_comments: Mozambique's Education Technology Plan (Plano Tecnológico da Educação, most recently updated in 2019, covering 2011-2026) sets out an explicit programme to build interoperability between the Ministry of Education's information systems (MINEDH and provincial/district directorates) and other government institutions, alongside a planned National Unique Citizen Number (NUIC) that would eventually cover student records. A DHIS2-based district education management information system pilot is running in two provinces. No operational integration currently exists between learner records, academic credentials or enrolment data and a national data exchange platform; the sector remains at the planning stage.

Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No evidence of electoral register integration with any data exchange platform. Score 1: not integrated.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) conflicted with the Comments, which already concluded a score of 1 (not integrated). Confirmed: no evidence found of the National Elections Commission's (CNE) voter register being integrated with a government data exchange platform; the only documented external data-sharing arrangement is a 2023 memorandum between the CNE and a civil society election-monitoring consortium (Mais Integridade) concerning electoral-process transparency, not identity verification or government service delivery. Revised Value Code to 1 (Not integrated), matching the evidence-based conclusion already present in Comments.
revised_comments: Mozambique's National Elections Commission (CNE) maintains its own voter registration data system, administered through the Technical Secretariat for the Administration of Elections (STAE), including biometric (fingerprint and photograph) capture. There is no evidence that the electoral register is technically integrated with a national government data exchange for identity verification, demographic analysis or service-delivery targeting. The only documented external data-sharing arrangement is a memorandum of understanding with a civil society election-monitoring consortium concerning transparency of the electoral process, which is unrelated to government-to-government data exchange.

Comments: No documented integration of employment/labor services with a national data exchange platform. Score 1: not integrated.

New evidence from a 2026 World Bank Program-for-Results appraisal document ('MozJobs' / Skills for Employment and Economic Transformation in Mozambique, P513981, estimated approval 20 May 2026) describes plans to upgrade and integrate the existing TVET-MIS and Labour Market Information System (LMIS), adding generative-AI analytics to anticipate labour-market demand. revised_comments: A World Bank Program-for-Results operation ('MozJobs', Skills for Employment and Economic Transformation, appraised in 2026) plans to upgrade and integrate Mozambique's existing Technical and Vocational Education and Training Management Information System (TVET-MIS) with the Labour Market Information System (LMIS), adding advanced analytics to improve labour-market matching. This integration is at the planning and design stage under the programme's results framework; there is no evidence of an operational data exchange currently linking job-seeker registries, unemployment insurance or public employment programme data across government systems.

Definition: Integration of driver's license registration and traffic offence data
Comments: No documented integration of driver licensing with a national data exchange platform. The Interoperability Law (Decree 67/2017) provides a framework for future integration. Score 1: not integrated.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) conflicted with the Comments, which concluded a score of 1 (not integrated), citing only the 2017 Interoperability Law (Decree 67/2017) as a framework for future integration. Fresh evidence found: in August 2025 INATRO (National Road Transport Institute) signed a memorandum of understanding with CEDSIF (the Ministry of Finance's shared IT systems centre, which already hosts other interoperable government systems such as e-INAS and e-Tributação) to host and digitally modernise INATRO's systems, and in December 2025/January 2026 INATRO launched a pilot digital road-traffic-offence monitoring centre in Greater Maputo (KOICA-funded). These are concrete steps toward eventual data-exchange integration but do not yet constitute operational integration with other government systems. Revised Value Code to 2 (Planned).
revised_comments: In August 2025, Mozambique's National Road Transport Institute (INATRO) signed a memorandum of understanding with CEDSIF, the Ministry of Finance's shared systems-hosting centre that already underpins other interoperable government platforms such as e-INAS and e-Tributação, to host and digitally modernise INATRO's driver-licensing and vehicle systems. Separately, a pilot digital road traffic-offence monitoring centre, funded by the Government of South Korea (KOICA), began operating in Greater Maputo in December 2025. These developments lay technical groundwork for future data exchange, but driver-licensing and traffic-offence data are not yet integrated with a national government data exchange platform.

Definition: Integration of social assistance programs, grant registries, beneficiary management systems
Comments: No documented operational integration of social protection with a data exchange platform. World Bank EDGE project supports foundational ID work that will eventually enable social protection targeting. Score 2: planned.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) conflicted with the Comments, which already concluded a score of 2 (planned). Confirmed and detailed by an ILO interoperability diagnostic of Mozambique's social protection information systems: the beneficiary management system (e-INAS) currently interoperates only with mobile-money providers (M-Pesa, eMola, Paycode) for payments, not with other government registers; a technical roadmap exists for future API/ETL-based data exchange between e-INAS, the civil registration system (e-RCEV), the pension system (SISSMO) and the tax authority (AT) via the National Unique Citizen Number (NUIC), but this is not yet operational, partly because NUIC is only issued to those born after 2017. A national social registry design process was initiated in 2024-25 with World Bank support. Revised Value Code confirmed at 2 (Planned).
revised_comments: Mozambique's social protection beneficiary management system (e-INAS, run by INAS) currently interoperates only with mobile-money providers (M-Pesa, eMola, Paycode) for benefit payments; it does not yet exchange data with other government registers. A technical roadmap sets out future API-based data exchange between e-INAS, the civil registration system (e-RCEV), the contributory pensions system (SISSMO) and the tax authority, keyed to the National Unique Citizen Number, but implementation is constrained because the NUIC is currently issued only to citizens born from 2017 onwards. A national social registry design process, supported by the World Bank, began in 2024-25 but is not yet operational.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No evidence of AI integrated into government data exchange systems. The World Bank/AfDB Data Governance Diagnostic (April 2025) makes no mention of AI in current data exchange infrastructure. An AI strategy is being developed under INTIC/World Bank/UNESCO support within the Information Society Policy to 2028. About 80% of Mozambicans were offline in 2024 (ITU). Systems are fragmented and rely on email/flash drives for data exchange. Score 1: no AI integration.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (0) conflicted with the Comments, which concluded a score of 1 (no AI integration). Fresh evidence found: INTIC published a first draft of Mozambique's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for public consultation (4 May - 4 June 2026), which post-dates the April 2025 Data Diagnostic that found no AI use in current data-exchange infrastructure. A separate, unrelated development is the Tax Authority's AI-based VAT fraud-detection programme (announced August 2025); this concerns the tax authority's own systems, not the cross-government data exchange, so it was not used to justify a higher score. Given the national AI strategy is still in draft/consultation and no AI is documented as integrated into the actual data exchange, revised Value Code is 2 (Planned) rather than 1 (No).
revised_comments: Mozambique's National Institute of Information and Communication Technologies (INTIC) published a first draft of a National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for public consultation between 4 May and 4 June 2026, signalling government intent to develop AI capability including for public-service delivery, though it is not specific to the government data exchange and remains in draft form. Separately, the Tax Authority has announced plans to deploy AI-based fraud detection and predictive analytics for VAT compliance, though this pertains to a single agency's systems rather than the cross-government data exchange. No AI is currently documented as integrated into Mozambique's data exchange infrastructure for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics across government systems.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: Mozambique has Right to Information Law (No. 34/2014) but enforcement is weak (21-day response often ignored per 2025 diagnostic). INTIC website publishes some documentation. National Data Governance Policy (zero draft 2, Nov 2025) includes transparency commitments. No public dashboard for data exchange operations. Score 2: low/limited disclosure.

revision_notes: Confirmed. Both originally cited sources were fetched and reviewed; their content matches the Comments. Additional corroboration found: GIZ (December 2025) reports that Mozambique's data governance reform process began in July 2025 and references the same Zero Draft 2 Data Governance Policy (November 2025), which includes transparency and accountability commitments but no public dashboard for data exchange operations. Score of 2 (Low - Limited Disclosure) confirmed; year updated to 2025 to reflect the most recent evidenced document (Zero Draft 2 Policy, November 2025). Value Name text differs slightly from the scale label but is cosmetic and does not affect the score.
revised_comments: Mozambique has a Right to Information Law (Law No. 34/2014), but enforcement is weak, with the mandated 21-day response period often ignored. INTIC publishes some documentation on its website, and the National Data Governance Policy (Zero Draft 2, November 2025), developed as part of a data governance reform process launched in mid-2025 with international partner support, includes commitments to transparency and accountability. However, there is no public dashboard or systematic annual reporting on data exchange operations, governance or data-sharing agreements. Overall transparency remains low, limited to occasional disclosures.
